detailed_rationale:
Arvind Fashions operates a portfolio of owned and licensed branded apparel and footwear franchises, distributed through exclusive brand outlets and multi-brand retail channels. Revenue growth has been consistent and real across the last four quarters (Jun-2025 +15.9% YoY, Sep-2025 +11.4%, Dec-2025 +14.5%, Mar-2026 +14.8%), broadly in line with our data's ~14% one-year growth figure and a step-up from the 3-year revenue CAGR of ~9%.

The key earnings-quality item to flag: Mar-2025 posted an outright net loss of -Rs.72 Cr on an unusual ~210% effective tax rate - a clear one-off tax/deferred-tax adjustment, not an operating collapse, and it should not be read as core profitability deteriorating. Its main practical effect is to badly distort the trailing 3-year ROE average (6.3%) relative to the current-year figure (14.1%), which is the more representative number once that single quarter's tax anomaly is set aside - a good example of why the 3-year metric needs the one-off called out rather than taken at face value. Excluding that quarter, underlying profit growth has still been choppy but directionally positive (Jun-2025 +78.6% YoY, Sep-2025 +24.4% YoY, Dec-2025 -23.4% YoY), consistent with a business still working through mix and cost normalization rather than one with a clean, steady earnings trend.

Leverage is elevated (D/E ~1.42x, Rs.1,336 Cr borrowings against Rs.943 Cr equity) - a real consideration for a consumer discretionary retailer, though a meaningful part of reported "borrowings" at Indian retail/EBO-heavy companies is often lease-liability accounting (Ind AS 116) rather than pure financial debt; I could not separate the two from the sources available, so I am flagging the leverage as a genuine watch-item without overstating it as distress. Promoter holding has drifted down slightly (36.78% to 35.10% since Mar-2024) but is broadly stable, and DII ownership (~25%) is healthy.

Reverse-DCF: at ~45.6x earnings against a current-year ROE of ~14.1% (ROCE ~19.6%) and consistent low-double-digit revenue growth, the multiple is rich relative to what a mid-teens-ROE apparel retailer has demonstrated - it requires either further margin expansion or sustained acceleration in growth to be earned back.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Hold on both lenses, with a notably high quality_score (72.8) despite the ROE volatility, likely reflecting solid ROCE and other balance-sheet factors. My own work agrees Hold is appropriate: growth is real and consistent, the Mar-2025 loss is a clearly identified one-off tax item rather than an operating problem, but the rich ~45.6x multiple against a mid-teens ROE and elevated leverage does not clear the bar for anything beyond Hold, and there is no methodology gap or coin-flip tension here warranting escalation.
summary: Arvind Fashions runs a portfolio of licensed and owned apparel brands through exclusive and multi-brand retail. Revenue has grown consistently in the low-to-mid teens, and a large loss in early 2025 was a one-off tax item rather than a business problem. Leverage is on the higher side and the stock is not cheaply valued relative to current profitability, so we rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Revenue growth has been consistent and genuine across the last four quarters (11-16% YoY), and current-year ROE (14.1%) and ROCE (19.6%) show a healthier underlying profitability trend than the distorted 3-year ROE average suggests once the Mar-2025 one-off tax hit is set aside. A diversified portfolio of licensed and owned apparel brands, plus healthy DII ownership (~25%), gives the business multiple levers for continued brand-level execution.
negative_para: Leverage is elevated (D/E ~1.42x) for a consumer discretionary retailer, and even excluding the one-off tax quarter, profit growth has been choppy quarter to quarter (down 23% YoY as recently as Dec-2025) rather than showing a clean upward trend. At ~45.6x earnings, the valuation already prices in a good deal of continued execution, leaving limited room if either growth decelerates or the elevated debt load becomes a larger drag in a higher-rate or weaker-consumer-demand environment.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~45.6x earnings against a current ROE of ~14.1% and ROCE ~19.6%, with consistent low-double-digit revenue growth, the multiple is rich relative to demonstrated returns - it requires further margin expansion or growth acceleration to be fully earned, rather than being clearly cheap or even plainly fair. Growth is below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
